request.input: So, based on what you told me, I should use the 3-second rule and start moving toward her within three seconds of seeing someone I'm interested in. Is that correct?

content.text:
**Yes, that is exactly correct.**

But here is the "why" behind it, because understanding the logic will help you actually stick to it when the nerves hit:

The 3-second rule isn't about the girl; **it is about your own brain.**

Between second 4 and second 30, your brain enters a phase called **"Over-Analysis."** This is where you start thinking:
* *"What if she's busy?"*
* *"What if she thinks I'm weird?"*
* *"What if I don't know what to say?"*
* *"Look at her body language, she probably doesn't want to be bothered."*

By the time you hit 10 seconds, you have built a mental wall so high that you've convinced yourself that approaching is a bad idea. You have essentially "talked yourself out of it."

**By moving within 3 seconds, you are bypassing the "Fear Center" of your brain and acting on instinct.**

### A Pro-Tip for implementing this:
Don't think about the *entire* conversation. If you think, *"I have to walk over there, start a conversation, be charming, and get her number,"* you will freeze.

**Break the 3-second rule into a "Micro-Goal":**
Your only goal for those first 3 seconds is to **physically change your location.** 

*   **Goal:** Move from Point A (where you are) to Point B (where she is).
*   **The Logic:** Once you are standing in front of her, your "social skills" (which you already said you are good at) will naturally take over. You don't need to plan the conversation; you just need to get your body into the position where the conversation can happen.

**Try this:** Next time you see someone, don't even think about what you're going to say. Just tell yourself, *"I'm just going to go stand near her,"* and move. The momentum will carry you the rest of the way.
